about: Which dates each WXPredict question has been scored on, so no rule is tested on dates it was found, tuned or looked at on. Every result in data/eval/wxpredict is registered here exactly once; tests/test_wxpredict_exposure_ledger.py checks it. A new result is registered in the same PR that commits it, and untouched_from moves past every date scored. Written 11 Oct 2026 (the Codex action plan of 11 Oct, section 2: one exposure ledger).
untouched_note: No WXPredict model, rule or control has been scored on an event date from 10 Oct. H2 and H3a scored 5-9 Oct on 12 Oct: the newest dates with every event's market definition, books, prints, winner, whole local day of hourly forecasts and station day (data/eval/wxpredict/coverage/coverage_2026-10-05_on_2026-10-12.json; 10 and 11 Oct had no archived book yet). The market residual's own October log loss, which its --dump run also computes (1-11 Oct), went to a scratch file and was neither read nor committed. Data volumes after 4 Oct were counted (trade prints a day, R46) without outcomes or prices being scored. The same-day YES pilot's development run (12 Oct) scored 13 Sep - 8 Oct; the remaining-day walk-forward run whose dump it read also computes that walk-forward's October log loss (1-11 Oct), which went to a scratch file and was neither read nor committed. 12 Oct, evening: the report-lag and same-day forecast tests (report_lag_2026-10-12.json, same_day_forecast_2026-10-12.json) scored the remaining-day model on 15 Sep - 11 Oct, so the untouched dates start 12 Oct, and H3a's forward dates move from 10 to 12 Oct.

questions.question: Does the remaining-day model whose rows count a station report 8 min after its reading (Aviation Weather's p90 receipt latency) instead of 20 min hit the venue's winning bucket more often and lose less log loss, on days it never saw?
questions.rule_marker: v1 rows count a station report 20 min after its reading
questions.verdict: Yes (12 Oct): 18,336 venue decisions, four weekly folds each fitted on the days before it. 09-16h local: hit 56.97% -> 59.19% (+2.2 points, 90% +1.7 to +2.8), log loss 1.0072 -> 0.9616 (-0.054 to -0.038); the market 65.98% and 0.8019. 15-16h: 81.19% -> 85.24% (+3.1 to +5.0 points); US (F) cities at 15-16h 71.50% -> 83.39%, the market 85.66%. 11-12h: hit +0.5 points (-0.7 to +1.8), log loss -0.029 (-0.043 to -0.015). The newest report the rows knew: 46 -> 31 min old at the median. Frozen as wxrd-v2 (data/models/wxrd).

questions.question: On days it never saw, does the remaining-day model refitted before each week beat the one frozen before the first, how far does a weekly refit move its ladders, and does averaging five seeds' ladders beat one seed?
questions.rule_marker: How steady is the remaining-day model, and what steadies it?
questions.verdict: 13 Oct, v2 table, 9,776 venue decisions 09-16h, v2_eval's four weekly folds. Refit against frozen at 14 Sep: hit 58.80% -> 59.20% (-0.03 to +0.91 points), log loss 0.9682 -> 0.9615 (-0.0113 to -0.0023). A weekly refit changes the top bucket on 16.8-17.9% of decisions (mean total variation 0.093-0.096), but two seeds on the same data change it on 17.2-17.9% (0.096-0.098): the churn is the model's own randomness. Five seeds averaged against one: hit 59.20% -> 60.27% (+0.74 to +1.45 points), log loss 0.9615 -> 0.9413 (-0.0240 to -0.0164), better in each of the four weeks. Frozen as wxrd-v3 (five seeds).

questions.question: Replaying a weekly refit of wxrd-v3 (five seeds averaged) whose candidate, fitted before the gate week, must not lose log loss to the serving model on that week before it serves the next: does it serve better than the fit frozen before the first gate, and what does it give up against the fit on every day before the served week?
questions.rule_marker: Would a weekly, gated refit of wxrd-v3 have served better?
questions.verdict: 13 Oct, v2 table, venue decisions 09-16h, v2_eval's four weeks. Three gates (15 Sep, 22 Sep, 29 Sep weeks): the candidate's log loss was at or below the serving model's each time (-0.0009, -0.0068, -0.0011), so all three were promoted; five-seed ladders moved a mean total variation of 0.050-0.052 a week (p90 0.105-0.111; top bucket changed on 9.2-10.9% of decisions), half the single-seed 0.093-0.096. Served on 22 Sep-11 Oct (7,149 decisions): gated against frozen before 8 Sep, hit 59.94% -> 60.22% (-0.19 to +0.77 points), log loss 0.9330 -> 0.9310 (-0.0069 to +0.0028): not shown better. The fit on every day before the served week against the gated one: hit 60.22% -> 60.93% (+0.38 to +1.06 points), log loss 0.9310 -> 0.9257 (-0.0087 to -0.0019). The week the strict gate holds back costs more than the gate protects: serve the newest fit, gate the procedure on the week the serving model never saw.
